title: Effect of biochar amendment on crop yield in tropical soils
research_question: Does biochar soil amendment increase crop yield in tropical regions compared to unamended controls?

population.description: Tropical field and greenhouse crops grown in biochar-amended soils

intervention.description: Biochar soil amendment (any feedstock, any pyrolysis temperature)

comparator.definition: Same crop grown without biochar addition

primary.description: Crop yield (grain yield, fruit yield, tuber yield, biomass)
primary.direction_of_interest: positive (biochar expected to increase yield, especially in tropics)

intervention: Biochar soil amendment (any feedstock and pyrolysis conditions)
primary_outcomes: Crop yield (grain yield, fruit yield, tuber yield, total biomass per unit area)
typical_effect_size: +25% yield increase in tropical soils (vs +10% in temperate)
important_moderators: Biochar feedstock type (wood, crop residue, manure, sewage sludge)
Soil pH (acidic vs neutral vs alkaline)
Climate zone (must be tropical or subtropical)
extraction_priorities: 1. CRITICAL: Extract yield for BOTH biochar treatment AND unamended control
2. Control = no biochar (unamended); Treatment = with biochar
3. If multiple rates tested, extract EACH rate vs same control separately
5. Record biochar feedstock, pyrolysis temperature, and application rate
6. Record study location to confirm tropical/subtropical setting
7. Focus on CROP YIELD, not soil properties
tc_confusion_warnings: Control is the NO BIOCHAR treatment
Some papers test biochar + NPK factorial — extract biochar+NPK vs NPK (isolate biochar effect)
Multiple application rates should be extracted as separate rows
Pot experiments may report g/pot or g/plant — extract as-is with unit noted
RESTRICT to tropical/subtropical locations — exclude temperate/boreal studies
Check paper location: Africa, South/Southeast Asia, Central/South America, Oceania tropics

search.seed_papers_description: Jeffery et al. 2017 (Environmental Research Letters, biochar crop yield meta-analysis with tropical/temperate subgroups)

inclusion_criteria: Primary experiment comparing biochar-amended vs unamended soil
Reports yield or biomass data (numeric means)
Study conducted in tropical or subtropical region
Biochar is the experimental variable (not confounded with other amendments)
Includes both biochar treatment and unamended control
exclusion_criteria: Study in temperate, boreal, or mediterranean climate
No yield or biomass data reported
Only reports soil properties without crop yield
Biochar used only as growing medium (soilless culture)

published_pooled_effect.notes: Tropical subgroup (k=527 observations, 62 publications, latitude <=35 degrees). Overall grand mean +13%. Text states 'crop yields significantly increase by approximately 25%' in the tropics. CI bounds read from Figure 1 forest plot (paper text gives only 'approximately 25%'; exact tabular values are in supplementary MetaWin output not directly accessible). Graphical reading from Figure 1: lower ~+15%, upper ~+35%. Temperate soils show approximately -3% (CI crosses zero). ERL fully open access (CC-BY). DOI: 10.1088/1748-9326/aa67bd. Published April 2017.
